stem: A client spends several hours each day performing repetitive handwashing rituals in response to intrusive contamination fears and has marked distress when unable to complete them. Which condition is most consistent with this pattern?

options.A: Social anxiety disorder, in which the core fear is scrutiny or embarrassment rather than contamination obsessions with washing rituals.
options.B: Body dysmorphic disorder, in which the central preoccupation is perceived appearance defects rather than contamination fears.
options.C: Obsessive-compulsive disorder, in which intrusive contamination obsessions can drive time-consuming cleaning or handwashing compulsions.
options.D: Generalized anxiety disorder, in which broad excessive worry occurs without repetitive compulsions performed in response to obsessions.

rationale: NIMH describes OCD as involving uncontrollable recurring thoughts (obsessions), repetitive behaviors (compulsions), or both. Fear of germs or contamination is a common obsession, excessive cleaning or handwashing is a common compulsion, and clinically significant OCD symptoms are often time-consuming, distressing, or interfere with daily life. C is correct.
educational_objective: Recognize obsessive-compulsive disorder when intrusive contamination obsessions are linked to time-consuming repetitive handwashing or cleaning compulsions with distress or impairment.
source_organization: National Institute of Mental Health (NIMH), NIH
source_document_title: Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder: When Unwanted Thoughts or Repetitive Behaviors Take Over
source_locator: What is OCD? and Signs and Symptoms: obsessions are intrusive/unwanted recurring thoughts; contamination fear is a common obsession; excessive cleaning/handwashing is a common compulsion. Recognizing OCD: symptoms are often >1 hour/day, distressing, and interfere with daily life.
source_claim_supported: Intrusive contamination fears coupled with repetitive time-consuming handwashing and marked distress are strongly consistent with OCD's obsession-compulsion pattern.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Psychosocial Integrity, printed p.10: provide care/education for acute and chronic psychosocial health issues; assess coping, promote therapeutic environment, use therapeutic communication and behavioral-management techniques.

audit_findings.exact_locator: NIMH What is OCD?, Signs and Symptoms, Recognizing OCD; NCSBN Psychosocial p.10 screenshot verified
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final item matches the source-defined obsession-compulsion link and clinically significant time/distress pattern without claiming a definitive diagnosis beyond the vignette's 'most consistent' framing.

distractor_audit.A: Incorrect because the core pattern is contamination obsession plus compulsion, not scrutiny fear.
distractor_audit.B: Incorrect because the preoccupation is contamination, not perceived appearance defect.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrect because the vignette includes a specific obsession and repetitive compulsion rather than broad worry alone.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only C explains the linked intrusive contamination fear and time-consuming handwashing ritual.
audit_findings.cueing: All alternatives are psychiatric diagnoses with discriminating core symptom patterns.
audit_findings.blueprint: Psychosocial Integrity — chronic mental-health issue recognition and behavioral manifestations.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Re-read current NIMH OCD guidance and rendered NCSBN p.10 page, then all choices, rationale, time burden and diagnostic-framing language. C remained uniquely correct.
